sentences.text: Thus, in view of above, this Tribunal finds that there is sufficient material on record to establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that has resulted into grievous injuries to the petitioner.

Issue no.1 is,
accordingly, decided in favour of petitioner.
ISSUE NO.2
Whether petitioner is entitled to compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
OPP 19.
In view of the finding on Issue no.1, petitioner is entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).

20. The present claim petitions pertain to injury and scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

entities.text: R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.
So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned

,
they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort, disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
21. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

4.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.

The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result Dar Tikshit Baliyan vs Mahesh Kumar And Anr on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15861597/

sentences.text: The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)

(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-Pecuniary Damages (general damages)
(iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v)
and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

sentences.text: Reimbursement of medical expenses:

It has been argued that out of the total bills of Rs. 3,50,000/-, the bills to the tune of Rs.
1,36,235/- have been reimbursed as the father of the injured works in Delhi Police.

It is, however,
stated that the petitioner had to incur the medical expenditure of Rs. 1,84,914/- from his own pocket.

He has placed on record medical bills Ex.PW2/2 of an amount of Rs.3,21,149/- but on his own contention that out of the said amount an amount of Rs.1,36,235/- have been reimbursed,
therefore he is awarded a compensation of Rs. 1,84,914/- under this head.
(ii) Pain, suffering and loss of amenities:
The petitioner / PW-2 proved that he suffered grievous injuries POST TRAUMATIC SKIN FLAP AVULSION RT. FOOT AND POST FASCIOTOMY WOUND LEFT LEG & other multiple injuries.

The petitioner received treatment at Panchsheel Hospital,
Yamuna Vihar, Delhi and thereafter from Max Super Specialty Hospital, Patparganj, Delhi where he remained hospitalized from 13.04.2019 to 25.04.2019 and from 24.07.2019 to 31.07.2019.

The petitioner has also suffered 26% permanent disability in relation to bilateral lower limbs so, there can be no doubt that he must have suffered pain and suffering, physical as well as mental, owing to this injury.

Keeping in view the extent and nature of injury suffered by the petitioner and duration of treatment taken by him, an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- is awarded to him towards mental and physical shock and pain.
(iii) Loss of Income during Treatment:
The petitioner/PW-2 deposed that he was a student.
He has stated that he used to impart tuitions and earning 15,000/- to 20,000/- per month.
His income is being assessed on the basis of minimum wages for non-matriculate person (from 1.10.2018 to 18.10.2019 )as applicable to Delhi as on date of accident.
The minimum wages of non-matriculate person from 1.10.2018 to 18.10.2019 (date of accident dated 13.04.2019) were Rs. 15,400/- p.m.

As per evidence brought on record, petitioner received treatment for his injuries in Panchsheel Hospital, Yamuna Vihar, Delhi, where first aid was given to him and thereafter he was taken to Max Super Specialty Hospital, Patparganj, Delhi, therefore, he might have been unable to work for about six months after the accident during the time when he was undergoing treatment.
Hence, petitioner is entitled to loss of income for period of six months from the date of accident, which is computed to Rs. 15,400 x 6 = Rs. 92,400/-.

(iv). Loss of Future Income : PW-1 Dr. Binod Kalita, Orthopedics Specialist, Jag Pravesh Hospital proved the Disability Certificate Ex.PW1/1, wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner suffered permanent disability to an extent of 26% in relation to bilateral lower limbs.
PW-1 testified that the petitioner can do his day to day activities apart from facing difficulty in squatting and running.
He can do brisk walking.
In view of this, the functional disability of the petitioner is ascertained to be 15% in relation to whole body for computation of loss of future income.
The multiplier of damages has to be determined as per Sarla Verma Vs. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121.
As per the deposition of PW-2, on the date of accident, his age was 18 years.
Accordingly, multiplier of 18 would be applicable in the present case.
The income of the petitioner has already been ascertained hereinabove to be Rs. 15,400/- per month.

sentences.text: The actual loss of future earnings after ascertaining functional disability of the petitioner to be 15% comes to Rs. 27,720/- (i.e. 15% of Rs. 1,84,800/-).

After applying the multiplier of 18, the total loss would be Rs. 4,98,960/- (i.e. Rs. 4,98,960/- =

Besides it, petitioner is also entitled for future compensation @ 40% in view of Pranay Sethi judgment.
Thus, the total loss of future income comes to Rs. 6,98,544/- (Rs. 4,98,960/- + 1,99,584/-) which is so awarded to the petitioner.
(v) Special Diet and Conveyance Charges:
Petitioner / PW-2 deposed that he incurred a sum of Rs.20,000/- on special diet and Rs.20,000/- on conveyance.
No document in respect of expenses incurred by him on special diet and conveyance has been filed on record.
Therefore, he must have incurred expenses on conveyance and special diet.
Hence, a sum of Rs.40,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.
(vi) Loss of marriage prospects:
It is undisputed fact that the petitioner was unmarried at the time of accident and is still unmarried.
Undoubtedly, with 26% permanent disability in bilateral lower limbs, the petitioner is bound to have difficulty in finding a suitable match and to enjoy his married life.
Keeping in view the hardship, the petitioner is likely to face, he is further awarded a compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- under this head.
(vii) Attendant Charges:

Petitioner / PW-2, in his affidavit, has deposed that he has suffered 26%
permanent disability in bilateral lower limbs, in the accident and he also needs an attendant for his assistant to help him to walk, day to day need and requirement for whole life.
Considering the fact that petitioner suffered grievous injuries, I may observe that he may have required assistance of family member as attendant at least for a period of six months.
He did not file any document regarding appointment of any attendant but as the evidence remained unrebutted, he is awarded compensation of Rs. 20,000/- towards Attendant charges.

sentences.text: 24 . LIABILITY:
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
The respondent no. 1 is the principal tort feasor being driver and respondent no. 2 is vicariously liable being owner of the offending vehicle.
However, the offending vehicle was insured at the time of accident and the insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured.

In the instant case, the insurance company has not been able to prove that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached / violated by the insured in as much as legal offer was filed by the Insurance Company.
Consequently, respondent no. 3 / Insurance Company is liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.
Interest on the award amount 25.
On perusing the record, it is seen that petitioner has conducted the proceedings diligently.
Hence, petitioner is entitled to interest @ 9% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
RELIEF 26.

This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs. 17,35,858/- (Rs. Seventeen Lakh Thirty Five Thousand Eight Hundred Fifty Eight Only) to the petitioner along with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of filing of petition till realization to be paid by the respondent no.3/ insurance company.

The insurer is also directed to give notice regarding deposit of the said amount to the petitioner and his counsel.

opennyai_summary.facts:
By this award, the instant claim petition under section 166 & 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
based on DAR (Detailed Accident Report), filed on behalf of the petitioner seeking compensation on account of injuries suffered by him in a motor vehicle accident, would be decided.
As a result of this, he fell down on the road and left rear wheel of the bus ran over his right foot due to which he sustained injuries i.e. POST TRAUMATIC SKIN FLAP AVULSION RT. FOOT AND POST FASCIOTOMY WOUND LEFT LEG and other multiple injuries.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. Upon completion of pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor, vide order dated 23.04.2019, framed the following issues:
i). Whether petitioner sustained injuries in motor accident caused by rash and negligent driving of driver of vehicle no. DL-1PC- 8386 i.e. by respondent no. 1 on 13.04.2019 at about 7:00 p.m. at C-Block, Yamuna Vihar, Bus Stand, Wazirabad Road, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS Gokalpuri?
OPP ii).
Whether petitioner is entitled to compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
Whether petitioner sustained injuries in motor accident caused by rash and negligent driving of driver of vehicle no. DL-1PC-8386 i.e. by respondent no. 1 on 13.04.2019 at about 7:00 p.m. at C-Block, Yamuna Vihar, Bus Stand, Wazirabad Road, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS Gokalpuri?

14. The fact that FIR has been registered and criminal proceedings have been initiated against the respondent no.1 by the police, are sufficient proof to conclude that respondent no.1 was negligent.
In the aforesaid case, Hon'ble Delhi High Court referred to the judgment titled as National Insurance Company Pvt. Ltd. v. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. (2008) 101 DRJ 645, wherein it was observed:

The respondent no.1 was the best witness, who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the testimony of the petitioner (PW2) regarding the above accident and its manner but he preferred not to enter into the witness box during the course of inquiry.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by him in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. v. Kamlesh, 2009(3) AD (Delhi)
310.
16.
On perusal of MLC, prepared by Max Hospital, it is evident that petitioner had suffered grievous injuries in RTA (road traffic accident).
17.
Besides above, it is settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However,
the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012,
Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530,
Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
Dar Tikshit Baliyan vs Mahesh Kumar And Anr on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15861597/
5 18.
Thus, in view of above, this Tribunal finds that there is sufficient material on record to establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that has resulted into grievous injuries to the petitioner.
In view of the finding on Issue no.1, petitioner is entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
20. The present claim petitions pertain to injury and scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.
21. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.
The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result Dar Tikshit Baliyan vs Mahesh Kumar And Anr on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15861597/
6 of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
As per the deposition of PW-2, on the date of accident, his age was 18 years.
The respondent no. 1 is the principal tort feasor being driver and respondent no. 2 is vicariously liable being owner of the offending vehicle.
However, the offending vehicle was insured at the time of accident and the insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured.
In the instant case, the insurance company has not been able to prove that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached / violated by the insured in as much as legal offer was filed by the Insurance Company.
